notes: Runner clicked for credits nearly every click all game, reaching 48 credits without installing anything, and never contested the remote while the Corp advanced and scored three agendas. The only real run was one R&D access via Liza.

Corp double-iced HQ but left R&D open early, so two House of Knives were stolen, and it spammed naked assets. Otherwise it played a coherent Jinteki damage plan: Neural EMP, Ronin for 3, and a Fetal AI trap that flatlined the Runner.

Strong opening with R&D pressure and an Archives steal, then four turns of clicking for credits at 20-32 credits while the Corp put up several unprotected remotes and discarded to Archives. It won only because Audacity dumped agendas into Archives.

Corp left HQ open for the first two turns (luckily without agendas there), then built economy with Hedge Fund and AAL and scored three agendas through Border Control. There were some excess draw clicks that led to discards.

Runner facechecked the remote and HQ without breakers early and let two agendas score from the remote, but then ran R&D every turn with Liza and took net damage to steal Obokatas. Tag management via repeated 2-credit removals was clunky but it won.

Corp clicked for credits almost every turn, never installed or scored an agenda, and kept agendas in HQ behind a single ice, so the Runner stole from HQ three times. It added only one remote ice and never improved its central defence.

Runner played Calling in Favors twice to no effect and lost Paperclip facechecking Ichi, but it kept pressure on R&D and paid through Fairchild to steal from the remote. It won against a collapsing Corp.

Runner spent every click running open R&D at 1 credit, mostly re-seeing the same top card, while sitting on 8 tags. It never played a card, built economy, or checked HQ or the remotes, and discarded every turn; it won only because R&D stayed unprotected.

Corp kept putting agendas into a remote behind a single Fairchild that the Runner broke three times. From turn 10 it clicked for credits for twelve turns up to 49 credits, never installing or scoring, while a broke, decked-out Runner eventually stole the win.
Corp left R&D unprotected for six turns under constant R&D runs, but scored agendas steadily from a Gatekeeper/Fairchild-protected remote and won. There were some passive credit clicks mid-game.

Twice Fairchild's last subroutine was resolved as core damage rather than end the run, which let the Runner steal Project Vitruvius and Megaprix Qualifier. Otherwise the Corp scored GFI, Megaprix and Vitruvius from remotes for a reasonable win.

Runner sat at 0-3 credits most of the game, Moshed away its own Black Orchestra and economy, and once ran the remote without the 1 credit Gagarin required to access. It still found steals through cheap Paperclip/Black Orchestra breaks.

Fairchild and Loki repeatedly resolved core damage instead of ending the run, which handed the Runner four steals (R&D twice, the 4-ice remote twice). The Corp also sat near 0 credits for most of the game and put Megaprix behind a single Magnet.

Runner ignored an advancing single-ice remote on turn 3 to play Sure Gambles. After losing Engolo it clicked for credits up to 32 without running while the Corp advanced and scored two more agendas over several turns.

Runner spent 2 credits giving Anansi Code Gate with Engolo and then could not break it, taking 4 net damage and emptying its grip. The final run into an unrezzed Jinteki remote ice on a 4-card grip ended in a flatline.

Corp installed an agenda behind unrezzed ice it could not afford to rez, and it was stolen. It then clicked for credits for nine straight turns up to 37 credits, discarding every turn, never adding ice to R&D or scoring while the Runner milked R&D.
Runner cleared most of the Hard-Hitting News tags at some cost and pressured open R&D and HQ, stealing three agendas from HQ and finishing through R&D. It could have hit HQ a bit earlier.

Corp left Fetal AI naked in a remote on turn 2 for a cheap steal, and later could not afford to rez the 4-ice remote protecting House of Knives. It did score Gila and used Snare/PE damage to win by flatline.
Corp played a sensible HB econ game with AAL, Spin Doctor and Seamless Launch, scoring three agendas from an iced remote. It made a few extra draw and credit clicks, but the plan was coherent.

Runner played Calling in Favors twice to no effect and burned Levy on turn 1, then clicked for credits up to 36 without installing a breaker or running remotes. The Corp scored freely; the only points came from one Archives check.
